name: window.focus
description: Bring the given window to the foreground. Returns the previously-foreground window's handle (so the caller can restore it later if desired).

handle.description: Window handle, e.g. 'win:0x1A2B', sourced from window.list / window.find.

prior_handle.description: Handle of the window that was foreground before the focus change. Empty string if there was no foreground window (rare).

focused_status.description: Outcome of the focus attempt. `ok`: the window is now foreground. `lock_held`: the OS foreground-lock restriction prevented the change (a process that hasn't received recent input is blocked from stealing focus). Mirrors window.move's `foreground_status` shape — same condition, success-with-status rather than ERR.

x-implementations.name: set_foreground_window
x-implementations.description: Win32 `GetForegroundWindow` (capture prior) + `SetForegroundWindow` (request focus). Subject to foreground-lock restrictions on NT 5+ (`SystemParametersInfo(SPI_GETFOREGROUNDLOCKTIMEOUT)`); denied requests return success with `focused_status: "lock_held"`.

windows-modern.description: SetForegroundWindow with GetForegroundWindow capture. Foreground-lock restrictions apply: a process that hasn't received recent input is blocked from stealing focus, returning success with `focused_status: "lock_held"`. The agent does NOT bypass the lock — callers can use `AllowSetForegroundWindow` from a privileged helper if needed.

windows-classic.description: SetForegroundWindow with GetForegroundWindow capture. NT 4 has no foreground-lock — the call always succeeds for the caller's permission level. NT 5 (Win 2000) onwards behaves like windows-modern.
